reading.body:
A point tagged as a data center in Siena, Italy is an accounting firm, not a data center.

The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no website. The name itself contains "Accounting," which identifies a bookkeeping practice serving local clients. The tag is best explained as a mapping error applied to the firm's own server room or network closet.

This matters for AI because facility counts drawn from open mapping data are not a measure of compute capacity. An accounting office runs office computers and perhaps a small file server. It does not offer colocation or cloud capacity, and it draws nothing like the power a real data center draws. Counting it alongside actual facilities inflates the apparent supply of buildings that could host compute.

The data does not say how many similar misclassifications exist elsewhere, and it does not cover the firm's actual IT footprint. It records one determination about one point, with the source being a tagging review dated 2026-09-04.
